summary: Alerts ceased for customer routes after long-running prefix-cache rewrite during model rollout
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that alerting rules attached to several production routes stopped generating notifications after we rolled out a model version that triggered a long-running prefix-cache rewrite job. Impact: ByteWave Health missed multiple production alerts (error-rate and latency SLO) for ~27 minutes during a business-critical window. Environment: prod (us-east-1), Dedicated pool id dp-07a9. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create route with prefix/KV caching enabled and alert rules on 95th latency and 5xx rate. 2) Trigger a model rollout that enables the new cache-preserve rewrite path (feature flag: cache/preserve-prefix-rewrite). 3) Observe the cache rewrite job running for >20 minutes; during this window, the alert evaluation engine shows constant series for affected routes and suppresses notifications due to dedupe/coalescing heuristics. Expected: Alerts should fire when evaluation windows cross SLO thresholds regardless of background cache maintenance. Actual: Alerts suppressed or delayed until rewrite completed and metrics returned to normal variance. Logs/observations: - Alert engine logs show repeated "coalesce: suppress duplicate outcome" entries for eval IDs. - Cache-worker logs show long-running prefix-rewrite batches and repeated touch/refresh events extending TTLs. - Customer traces show API requests returning elevated latencies concurrently with suppressed alert notifications. Attachments: Grafana panel snapshots, relevant trace IDs, alert evaluation trace IDs (provided to engineering).

investigation_notes: Alert evaluation engine coalescing behavior: dedupe window (300s) checks for identical series fingerprints; if samples are identical or timestamps monotonically advance without variance, notifications suppressed.

Cache rewrite job touches existing prefix entries and rewrites TTLs which results in sample timestamp updates on the metrics index. This produces series that appear unchanged except for timestamp, triggering dedupe logic.

Reproduced in staging: enabling cache/preserve-prefix-rewrite produced suppressed alerts for synthetic route with alert rule identical to customer's. Disabling the preserve behavior restored alert firings.
Query traces: alert-eval trace id ae-20260312-09 shows coalesce decision path at alert-eval service commit point; stacktrace indicates coalesce check in handler coalesce.go:line 218.
Related PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4123 introduces the cache-preserve rewrite and touches TTL semantics; PR author: @m-torres.
resolution: Workaround (applied 2026-03-13 02:40 UTC): Disabled cache/preserve-prefix-rewrite flag for ByteWave's dedicated pool which allowed alerts to re-fire immediately. Customer confirmed alerts resumed.

Permanent fix (in progress): Change alert-eval dedupe logic to ignore sample-timestamp-only updates that are attributable to cache maintenance events. Patch PR targeting alert-eval service (WIP) references platform PR 4123 — engineering has a code branch and tests added.

Postmortem action items: 1) Add an event marker for cache-maintenance touches so alert-eval can filter them (owner: Platform Eng, due 2026-03-20). 2) Add an observability metric to detect suppressed-alert clusters during cache maintenance (owner: SRE, due 2026-03-17). 3) Communicate change and recommended rollout practice for cache-preserve rewrites to CS and Solutions Engineers.
Customer communication: Sent interim incident summary and confirmed ByteWave will monitor external aggregator until permanent fix is deployed.
